## The Problem: AI Amnesia {.smaller}

**Every time you open a new chat, the AI starts from scratch.**

::: {.incremental}
- **Constant Re-explaining**: You spend the first ten minutes rebuilding context — your project, your conventions, your decisions, your background. Then the session ends. Next time, you do it again.
- **Nothing Accumulates**: The model is sharp but stateless. That statelessness is the real ceiling, not the model's intelligence.
- **Enterprise Solutions Are Overkill**: Companies use RAG and vector databases, but for personal use they are overbuilt, opaque, and fragile. You cannot debug a cosine similarity score by opening a markdown file.
:::

---

## How This Started {.smaller}

**A conversation about markdown files sent me down a rabbit hole.**

::: {.incremental}
- A conversation with a professor about markdown note-taking workflows was the spark. I went home that night and started building.
- I was managing complex, multi-threaded technical work and kept hitting the same wall: re-explaining context every single session.
- The result is the **Neural Vault** — a structured Obsidian vault that works alongside Claude's native memory to give you persistent, portable, project-specific context across every AI session.
- No vector database. No infrastructure. Just markdown files, a disciplined workflow, and a few shell scripts.
:::

---

## Inside the Obsidian Brain {.smaller}

**Your knowledge, connected and readable by both you and the AI.**

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="45%"}
<br>

- **Inbox**: Raw capture — quick, unorganized thoughts.
- **Wiki**: Structured knowledge the AI helped you write.
- **Meta**: `About_Me`, Index, Prompts, and Session Log.
- **Archive**: Deprecated notes, kept for history.
- **Agent Sandbox**: A messy workspace for AI agents — kept separate so your vault stays clean.
:::

## Standing on Each Other's Shoulders {.smaller}

**Karpathy and I arrived at the same problem from different directions — and solved different halves of it.**

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Andrej Karpathy
*The AI as Librarian*

Karpathy published his LLM Knowledge Base method in April 2025. His core insight: have the LLM incrementally build and maintain a persistent wiki from raw sources.

**What he solved:**

- The `raw/` → `wiki/` ingestion pipeline
- LLM-written, human-curated notes
- Health checks to find gaps and inconsistencies
- Web Clipper ingestion for articles and links
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### What I Built — The Neural Vault
*The AI as Collaborator*

I built the core of this system independently, starting from a different problem: not how to store knowledge, but how to **load it into an active session**.

**What I built independently:**

- **Two-layer memory split**: separating Claude's ambient memory (who you are) from a structured wiki (what you know) — Karpathy's system doesn't address this at all
- **Context Injection Protocol**: a formal, repeatable prompt template — a structured handshake between your vault and the model
- **`COMMIT:` flag**: I ask Claude to mark insights worth saving mid-session, so nothing gets lost
- **Auto-save daemon**: every file save = a silent git commit. Zero manual steps. Fully reversible.
:::

::::

## The Ultimate Setup: Both Together {.smaller}

**Use Karpathy's method to *build* the vault. Use AJ's method to *load* it.**

![](context_engineering.png){width="68%" fig-align="center"}

::: {.fragment}
<div style="font-size: 0.85em; color: #475569; text-align: center; margin-top: 10px;">
Karpathy fills the vault with knowledge from what you read. AJ's system loads that vault into every active work session — so the AI already knows your goals, your style, and what you decided yesterday.
</div>
:::

## The Result: Compounding Intelligence {.smaller}

**The system gets better every time you use it.**

::: {.incremental}
- **Stop Re-explaining**: The AI always knows your context because you hand it the ready-made summary.
- **Ideas Are Never Lost**: Every good session turns into a permanent note in your notebook.
- **You Own Everything**: Plain markdown files on your computer. No vendor lock-in. Switch models tomorrow — the vault comes with you.
- **An Investment in the Future**: The notebook you build today will make whatever AI you use tomorrow smarter and more aligned with you.
:::

. . .

> *"The vault you build today is the training set for the model you run tomorrow."*
